sources.title: CompTIA SecAI+ — Overview, learning comparison, Buy Now details and Resources/FAQs
sources.note: Official offer: CY0-001, launched 17 February 2026. CertMaster Perform is 30–60 hours with instruction, assessments and simulated/live labs. US prices observed: training $508; complete bundle $628 including exam and retake; exam alone $298. Twelve months of training access. Exam: up to 60 questions, 60 minutes, passing score 600/900. Recommended 3–4 years IT and about two years cybersecurity experience. Public pages describe applied work on threats, controls, data, monitoring and automation.

sources.title: CompTIA CY0-001 objectives, document version 2.0 — publisher PDF hosted by ONLC
sources.note: All 13 pages reviewed, including 15 objectives, acronym and example equipment/software lists. Domains: AI concepts 17%; securing AI 40%; AI-assisted security 24%; GRC 19%. Scope covers model/prompt/data/lifecycle fundamentals; threat modelling; system/access/data controls; monitoring; attacks and mitigations; security tools; attacker uses; automation; governance, risk and compliance. PDF exam logistics remain TBD: use current official product page for those. Acronyms and equipment lists do not earn teaching credit.

sources.title: Official CertMaster Perform learning design
sources.note: Instruction, videos, interactive content, simulated/live practice and assessments; resources index also inspected. This establishes delivery method, not evidence that every framework skill is practised.

sources.title: Avantus — detailed SecAI+ teaching outline
sources.note: Reviewed all six modules and their numbered subtopics. Primary evidence for this provider's taught syllabus; corroboration for the common SecAI+ curriculum, not proof that all providers deliver identical content. Modules cover AI/data, threat modelling and controls, access/data/monitoring, lifecycle and attacks, security uses and misuse, and GRC.

sources.title: Compendium — authorized SecAI+ course outline and activities
sources.note: All six PDF pages reviewed. Named practice includes prompting and bias, RAG, integrity checks, threat analysis, Azure deployment/security, access requests, data sanitization, AI auditing, injection tests, vulnerability analysis, deepfake recognition, scripting, document analysis, workflow automation, governance design, risk assessment and compliance reporting. Useful evidence of practice in an authorized course; not a guarantee of these exact labs in the official self-paced product.

sources.title: ISC2 Building AI Strategy Certificate — complete bundle
sources.note: Six courses, 16 hours/CPEs; $640 regular/$512 member; 60-day access. Course certificate and badge require learning, assessment and evaluation. Reviewed overview, learning outcomes, audience, completion conditions and all six included-course links. A professional-development certificate, not a separate ISC2 professional certification exam.

sources.title: ISC2 AI for Cybersecurity — 3 hours
sources.note: Product details introduce AI applications and lifecycle alongside traditional and AI-specific defence. Outcomes concern recognizing AI attacks, describing mitigations and identifying threat tools. Video/text, case-study activities and assessment. Public synopsis does not enumerate attack categories, controls or the case exercises.

sources.title: ISC2 AI Security: Managing Overconfidence — 3 hours
sources.note: Addresses blind spots, automation bias, data-driven identification of tool weaknesses, critical assessment/refinement of outputs, and balancing AI with human judgement. Discusses adapting models and maintaining human accountability. Video/text, learning activities and assessment; exercise specifications are not public. Recommended familiarity with cybersecurity and AI capabilities.

sources.title: ISC2 Aligning with Global AI Regulations — 2 hours
sources.note: Compares AI security frameworks and standards, their guiding principles, alignment and implications for development/deployment. Case-study activities and assessment. The published outcomes do not identify EU literacy duties or HKMA/MAS requirements, so regional mapping cannot receive full credit.

sources.title: ISC2 Foundations of AI — 4 hours
sources.note: Definitions, terminology, technologies, subtypes, applications and functions/impact. Video/text, case studies and assessment. Public outcomes do not specify agent harnesses, memory, tools, MCP, Skills, provider trade-offs or context windows.

sources.title: ISC2 Planning for Secure by Design AI — 2 hours
sources.note: Connects cybersecurity to AI governance and risk; identifies relevance across leadership, operations and development; applies security through the lifecycle; considers organizational AI use, ethical/fair use and maturity. Case-study activities and assessment. Specific agent control designs and deployment exercises are not described.

sources.title: ISC2 Evolving Cybersecurity Workforce — 2 hours
sources.note: Job changes, adaptation and training, employees' use of LLM productivity tools, privacy compliance, human accountability and ethical oversight. Product detail adds privacy impact assessments, reviews and audits. Video/text, learning activities and assessment. No public agent-supervision ratios, authority tiers or junior-development programme.
